name: ESSAI 2026
venue: European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence, Vienna, Austria
description: The 2026 European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence (ESSAI) is a one‑week program for PhD students and young researchers, held in Vienna, Austria. It offers introductory and advanced AI courses, specialized tutorials on Bilateral AI and Digital Humanism, and extensive networking opportunities across six parallel tracks. The school also includes a rich social program, such as a reception at the Vienna City Hall, to foster community among participants.

name: OpenEuroLLM Winter School
venue: Skeikampen conference hotel, near Oslo, Norway
description: The 2026 Winter School on Multilinguality in LLM Development and Evaluation is organized by the Nordic Language Processing Laboratory and the University of Oslo in Norway. It targets NLP researchers, especially those from EuroHPC consortium countries and doctoral students, and focuses on multilingual large language models, evaluation methods, and data curation. The event is held at the Skeikampen conference hotel north of Oslo, offering subsidized participation, bus transfers from Oslo Airport, and includes hands‑on talks, walks, and networking opportunities.

name: Probabilistic AI School
description: The Probabilistic AI School 2026 will take place in Vilnius, Lithuania from August 3 to August 7, 2026. It aims to provide an inclusive educational environment featuring state‑of‑the‑art machine learning and artificial intelligence topics. The programme invites students, academics, industry professionals and AI enthusiasts to learn, collaborate, and network.

name: BMVA Computer Vision Summer School
description: The 29th BMVA Computer Vision Summer School will be held at Durham University in Durham, England, UK. It offers an intensive five‑day program of lectures and lab sessions that cover a broad spectrum of computer‑vision topics presented by leading researchers from the UK and abroad. The school is designed for graduate students and early‑career researchers seeking hands‑on experience and exposure to current advances in the field.

name: Oxford Machine Learning Summer School 2026
venue: Oxford Machine Learning School, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The MLx Health & Bio programme is part of the Oxford Machine Learning School’s 2026 summer offering. It runs from 10 to 13 July 2026 in a hybrid format, bringing together researchers and practitioners to explore how representation learning and generative AI address challenges in healthcare and biomedical sciences. Participants engage with topics such as AI in imaging, computational biology, real‑world health data, multi‑omics, drug discovery, and population health epidemiology.

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning (RPL) Summer School
venue: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden
description: The RPL Summer School 2026 is a six‑day event organized by the Department for Robotics, Perception and Learning at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm, Sweden. It brings together doctoral and postdoctoral researchers to discuss topics such as machine learning, computer vision, robotics, human‑robot interaction, planning and decision making through keynotes, industry talks, brainstorming sessions and student presentations. The program is hosted at the Happy Tammsvik resort, offering participants accommodation, meals and various indoor and outdoor activities to foster collaboration and generate concrete research ideas.

name: Machine Learning Crash Course at MALGA
description: The MLCC2026 Summer School – Machine Learning Crash Course – provides an introduction to fundamental machine‑learning concepts and algorithms. It is aimed at undergraduate and graduate students, as well as professionals, and is open to participants from any university after a selection process. The five‑day in‑person program in Genoa combines theoretical lectures with hands‑on lab sessions and includes a final test consisting of notebook work and a report.

name: UK Robotics Summer School
venue: National Robotarium, Heriot-Watt University, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
description: The UK Robotics Summer School is a five‑day event held at the National Robotarium, Heriot‑Watt University in Edinburgh. It offers expert‑led lectures, tutorials, industry talks and hands‑on experience with state‑of‑the‑art robotics technology, targeting master’s‑level students and industry practitioners. Participants can network with academics and industry leaders while enjoying refreshments, a special dinner, and a collaborative learning environment.

name: International Summer School for Advanced Studies on Biometrics, Behavior, and Vision
description: The 2027 Biometrics Summer School takes place at Hotel Dei Pini in Alghero, Sardinia, Italy. It focuses on the impact of agentic AI and vision foundation models on biometrics, covering machine learning, image understanding, signal analysis, neuroscience, robotics, forensic and digital forensics. The program is aimed at PhD students, post‑docs, researchers, forensic examiners, police officers and other professionals, offering keynote lectures, hands‑on sessions, and scholarships in a scenic Mediterranean setting.

name: Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal (ELS) aspects of AI and AS at Umeå University
description: The Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal aspects of AI and Autonomous Systems brings together researchers and students at Umeå University in Sweden. It offers lectures, multidisciplinary hands‑on training, a poster session, and a social program to explore the societal implications of AI and autonomous technologies. Participants can network with experts while receiving guidance on ethical, legal, and policy challenges in the field.

name: Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM 2026)
description: The ACM Europe Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM’27) will be held from 1–5 February 2027 in the Vercors mountains near Grenoble, France. The school targets PhD students and early‑career researchers, offering lectures, hands‑on sessions and informal networking on topics such as computer vision, speech processing, affective computing and human‑robot interaction. Set in a mountain setting, the programme aims to foster cross‑disciplinary exchange, collaborations and a broad perspective on socially intelligent systems.

name: Northern Lights Deep Learning Winter School
venue: UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Tromsø, Norway
description: The 2027 Northern Lights Deep Learning Conference includes a Winter School held from 11 to 15 January in Tromsø, Norway. The Winter School focuses on recent advances in deep learning, covering topics such as image classification, object detection, segmentation, time‑series prediction, and speech recognition. It is aimed at researchers and practitioners who want to exchange ideas, build collaborations, and learn cutting‑edge techniques from international experts.

name: Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS)
description: The 7th Annual Nepal AI School is an 11‑day intensive in‑person program held at Kathmandu World School in Kathmandu, Nepal. It offers a broad AI curriculum ranging from fundamental mathematics and statistics to cutting‑edge topics such as geometric deep learning, generative modeling, world models, and neuro‑symbolic AI, with lectures, labs, and project work. The school targets senior undergraduates, graduate students, PhD candidates, faculty, and industry professionals from South Asia and beyond.

name: EEML Summer School
description: The Eastern European Machine Learning Summer School takes place in Cetinje, Montenegro from 27 July to 1 August 2026. It brings together leading researchers from academia and industry to deliver lectures and tutorials on modern machine‑learning methods and their applications. The program targets students and early‑career researchers in the region, offering networking opportunities and exposure to cutting‑edge AI research.

name: Mediterranean Summer School
venue: Mediterranean Machine Learning Summer School, Barcelona, Spain
description: The Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School is a five‑day program held in Barcelona, Spain, offering keynotes, lectures, and practical sessions led by international AI experts. It targets doctoral and outstanding master students, as well as academics and practitioners, focusing on topics such as computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, reinforcement learning, and ethics in machine learning. The school emphasizes diversity, networking, and knowledge transfer, providing opportunities for poster presentations, scholarships, and informal interactions with speakers and industry partners.

name: AthNLP Summer School 2026
description: The Athens Natural Language Processing Summer School 2026 (AthNLP) is a week‑long intensive program focused on recent advances in NLP research and applications. It is hosted on the campus of NCSR Demokritos in Athens, Greece, and is jointly organized by several research institutes and universities, including RC Athena, NCSR Demokritos, Athens University of Economics and Business, Heriot‑Watt University, and the ELLIS‑Manchester partnership. The school targets graduate students and early‑career researchers, offering lectures, hands‑on tutorials, and networking opportunities, and it also supports the concurrent 14th EETN Conference on Artificial Intelligence.

name: Advanced Artificial Intelligence: GenAI & Deep Unsupervised Learning
venue: Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: AI For Finance summer school is offered by Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, as part of the 2027 Oxford Summer Programmes. It targets STEM students with intermediate experience in AI and machine‑learning who are interested in finance applications and are considering graduate study or research. The programme can be taken either residentially or online and runs from 28 June to 16 July 2027, providing hands‑on learning on AI techniques for financial data.

name: LUT Summer School
description: LUT Summer School is a one‑week intensive program that offers courses on sustainability, climate action, marketing, management, and inventive thinking, combining business and technology perspectives. It is aimed at bachelor’s and master’s students from any university, with a mix of online instruction and a on‑campus week at the Lappeenranta campus, complemented by social activities in Finnish nature. The programme includes workshops, group work, and networking events, providing both academic learning and cultural experiences.

name: 1st Internationa School on the Cognitive, Ethical, and Societal Dimensions of AI - AIces
description: AIces 2026 is the first International School on the Cognitive, Ethical and Societal Dimensions of Artificial Intelligence, held in Porto, Portugal. The program targets graduate and postgraduate students as well as industry practitioners, offering parallel courses, a symposium, and open debates on AI cognition, ethics, and societal impact. It combines face‑to‑face interaction with live online participation, and all lectures are recorded and available for 45 days after the event.

name: Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI
venue: Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications (INPT), Rabat, Morocco
description: The AI Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI is a five‑day immersive program held at the Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications in Rabat, Morocco. It offers theoretical lectures, hands‑on labs, and project mentorship by world‑renowned experts, aiming to equip young researchers, Ph.D. students and professionals with cutting‑edge AI knowledge. The school also emphasizes networking and leadership development to foster the next generation of AI leaders in Morocco.

name: AI4Science Summer School
description: The 2nd Summer School on Advancing Scientific Discovery with AI takes place in Caen, Normandy, France in 2025. It focuses on applying AI techniques such as machine learning, generative models, and AI‑driven experimental design to accelerate scientific research across various domains, with hands‑on workshops and case studies led by experts. The program is aimed at PhD students, post‑doctoral researchers and scientists familiar with mathematical modelling, numerical computation and Python programming.
